whats_next.text: Deciding how the Auditor, the system that checks this project's own work, should be credited, and how far its own authority should extend if it's ever given more than a screen to write to.

A different AI model, on different software, has never actually tried to pick this project up cold and run it the way Claude Code does. The instructions are believed ready for that test — they just haven't been put in front of a stranger yet.

A new AI tool joined the project, took one look at how much has to be re-read every single session, and proposed streamlining it. The first round of fixes — cleaning up duplicated content, automating the tedious parts of closing a session — is built and working; deciding how much further to take it is still open.

recent_catches.description: a filename that broke the index-completeness checker's own regex, caught live rather than assumed working, and a separate pre-existing gap in the wider `_messages/` corpus (43 files missing generated footers) surfaced by running the generator against the whole bundle instead of just the new batch.

three real bugs caught by actually running new code against live data before trusting it: a path-resolution mismatch between PowerShell's working directory and .NET's file APIs that silently wrote a stray file; a doubled blank line from an off-by-one in a text-insertion script; and a missing exit code that masked success as failure when scripts were composed together, which also turned out to be a latent bug in already-shipped code (`generate-stats-data.ps1`) that had simply never been exposed before.

Running the new stats-generation logic against live data caught two real bugs before they shipped: a PowerShell method overload that doesn't resolve on this version, and an empty list silently serializing to the wrong JSON shape — the same class of bug the page's own growth-history logic had already been built to avoid once before.
